_comment: Port life: what a visiting captain can do at a happening (chain_only: started from the port screen's Town tab, see data/port_life.json), and arrival events that grow out of how the town is (town.* keys) and how it sees you.

life_festival.title: {port} makes merry
life_festival.text: Fireworks over the harbour, a procession with a saint (or a bull, or a giant made of straw), and a crowd that will cheer anyone who gives it a show.

choices.result: Three shots, three oranges off the post. The crowd carries you round the square.
choices.fail_result: You miss the post entirely. Your entry fee buys the winner a drink.

choices.text: Give the crew a night ashore
choices.result: They come back at dawn, broke, hoarse and happy.

choices.text: Pay for a feast for the whole town
choices.result: Roast pigs on every corner, and your name on every tongue.

life_fair.title: The fair
life_fair.text: Bales of Rouen linen and Seville wine stacked to the eaves, mule trains from the mines, bankers changing silver at the church door, and more sharpers than honest men.

choices.result: You beat a Sevillan factor down to a price he'll regret.
choices.fail_result: The factor smiles all the way through. You've paid full price.

choices.text: Buy the moneylenders a dinner and listen
choices.result: Somebody important owes somebody else a great deal, and you know who.

choices.text: Sign on seamen paid off from the fleet
choices.result: Deep-water men, used to long voyages.

choices.text: Keep your purse in your shirt and go back aboard

life_bread_riot.title: Bread riots
life_bread_riot.text: The market square is a mob: women waving empty baskets, men with cudgels, militia with bayonets fixed and no idea what to do. Your hold has food in it, and everyone knows ships carry food.

choices.text: Sell a whole cargo of food at a fair price
choices.result: Your boats ply between ship and quay until dark. By morning there's bread in the shops, and your name on every street corner.

choices.text: Sell your provisions at a fair price
choices.result: They queue at your boat all afternoon. An old woman kisses your hand, and the square grows quieter.

choices.text: Sell them at what hunger will pay
choices.result: A fortune for salt pork. They'll remember your face, and not fondly.

choices.text: Help the militia clear the square
choices.result: A volley over their heads, and your men with cudgels. The square empties.
choices.fail_result: A flying cobblestone finds your head before the square is clear.

life_ball.title: The governor's ball
life_ball.text: Candles by the hundred, a string band sawing at a minuet, and {gov} receiving guests at the top of the stairs. A planter's wife looks you up and down; two merchants stop talking when you pass.

choices.result: {gov} laughs at your stories and asks you to call again. A favour freely given is a favour owed.
choices.fail_result: You tread on the feet of {gov}'s partner in the minuet. Twice.

choices.result: Planters play deep and badly. You leave with their sugar money.
choices.fail_result: Planters play deep and well, it turns out.

choices.text: Slip away and listen at the study door
choices.result: Letters on the desk that {gov} would not want read aloud.
choices.fail_result: A footman finds you with your ear to the keyhole.

choices.result: Contacts, introductions, and an idea of who's buying.

life_hanging.title: Hanging day
life_hanging.text: Three on the cart, hands tied, one still defiant. The crowd jeers; a parson reads; the hangman tests his ropes. Your crew are watching you as much as the gallows.

choices.result: It takes a long time. The men are quiet that night.

choices.text: Bribe the hangman for one life
choices.result: The rope 'breaks'. By the custom of the place, whoever the rope won't hang goes free, and {condemned} goes free into your crew.

choices.text: Cut {condemned} down tonight, from the gibbet
choices.result: One guard runs, one is persuaded. The Brethren will sing of it.
choices.fail_result: The guard raises the alarm. You lose two hands getting back to the boats.

life_captains_table.title: A captain's table
life_captains_table.text: {cap} has the best table in the tavern, a bottle of good Madeira, and half their crew around them. They look up as you come in.

choices.text: Buy a round and talk shop
choices.result: By the third bottle you're old friends, and you know every weak timber in their ship.
choices.fail_result: A joke lands badly. Knives aren't drawn, quite.

choices.text: Ask what they've seen on the sea lanes
choices.result: They let slip an anchorage that isn't on your chart.
You take their money, and they take it hard.
choices.fail_result: They take your money, and laugh about it.

choices.result: Tables go over. Now everyone knows there's bad blood between you.

town_beggars.title: Beggars on the quay
town_beggars.text: {port} has fallen on hard times. Beggars line the quay: sailors with no ship, a widow with three children, a soldier with one leg.

choices.result: Blessings follow you up the quay.
Three of them are aboard before you've finished speaking.

town_patron.title: A rich man's errand
town_patron.text: Business is booming in {port}, and a merchant with more money than time wants a dependable captain to carry letters of credit to his partners. Word is you can be trusted.

choices.result: Easy money, and a friend in the counting house.

town_curfew.title: Curfew
town_curfew.text: {port} is close to revolt. The militia has proclaimed a curfew: any sailor in the streets after dark goes to the stocks.

choices.text: Keep the crew aboard after dark
choices.result: A long dull evening of watching the town's lights.
One ends up in the stocks and isn't let out before you sail.

town_welcome.title: A welcome
town_welcome.text: Word of your coming has reached {port} ahead of you. People wave from the quay; a boy runs to tell the tavern keeper; the harbour master raises a hat.

choices.text: Doff your hat to the crowd
choices.result: The crew walk a little taller ashore.

town_ballads.title: Ballads
town_ballads.text: Children in {port} are singing a ballad about you: your cruelty, your gold, and how you'll hang one day. Their mothers drag them indoors as you pass.

choices.text: Toss them a coin for the next verse
choices.result: The next verse is worse. The crew love it.
They scatter.

town_war_widows.title: The widows' fund
town_war_widows.text: The war has filled {port}'s churchyard with sailors who never came home. The parish is collecting for their widows, and the churchwarden has an eye on you.

choices.result: Your name goes in the parish book.
A nod from the churchwarden.

life_festival_bravo.title: A swordsman in the crowd
life_festival_bravo.text: A local swordsman, all lace and swagger, steps out of the crowd and challenges any foreign captain to show what they're made of. The crowd turns to look at you.

choices.text: Draw and give them a show
choices.result: Three passes and the bravo's blade is in the fountain. The crowd roars.
choices.fail_result: The bravo is better than they look. You leave with a cut and a lesson.

choices.result: The crowd laughs with you, not at you.

life_festival_regatta.title: The boat race
life_festival_regatta.text: A race of ships' boats across the harbour, for a purse put up by the merchants. Every crew in port is entering, and yours are already arguing about who pulls stroke.

choices.result: Your boat crosses the line a length ahead. The crew won't stop talking about it.
choices.fail_result: Fourth, behind a fishing boat. The entry fee is gone.

choices.result: The favourite wins, as favourites do.

life_fair_sharper.title: The thimblerig
life_fair_sharper.text: A sharper at the fair has taken a week's pay off half your crew with three cups and a pea, and is now working on the rest.

choices.text: Show the crowd how the trick is done
choices.result: The pea is under the sharper's fingernail. The crowd gets its money back, and so does your crew.
choices.fail_result: The sharper's friends are bigger than you'd thought. You pay to be left alone.

choices.text: Tell the crew it serves them right

life_press_bargain.title: A bargain with the press
life_press_bargain.text: The lieutenant of the press gang is short of his quota. He offers you the King's bounty for any hands you can spare, no questions asked about who they are.

choices.text: Hand over three of the worst
choices.result: The men see it done. They'll remember.

choices.text: Tell him your men are your own
choices.result: The crew cheer you up the gangway.

life_press_rescue.title: Taken by the press
life_press_rescue.text: Two of your hands were taken by the press gang last night and are locked in the guardhouse with a dozen others, waiting for a navy boat.

choices.result: A door kicked in, a sentry knocked down, and fourteen men running for the boats. Yours, and some new volunteers.
choices.fail_result: The guard turns out. You get away, but your two stay where they are.

choices.text: Buy them back from the lieutenant
choices.result: Paperwork, a purse, and your men are home by dinner.

choices.text: Leave them to the King's service
choices.result: The crew don't forget a captain who leaves men behind.

life_riot_warehouse.title: The hoarder's warehouse
life_riot_warehouse.text: The mob has found a merchant who has been holding back grain to drive the price up. They're at his warehouse doors with a beam, and the militia is nowhere.

choices.text: Help them break it open and share it out
choices.result: Sacks pass hand to hand down the street. Some of them end up in your boat.

choices.text: Stand in the doorway with your officers
choices.result: The crowd backs off. The merchant pays handsomely, and hates you for seeing his fear.
choices.fail_result: The beam comes through the door, and over you.

choices.text: Buy the grain and sell it at a fair price
choices.result: You pay the hoarder his price and sell at cost from the warehouse steps. The riot ends there.

life_ball_insult.title: An insult
life_ball_insult.text: A young officer of the garrison, flushed with wine, says loudly that the governor lets any sea-thief in off the street these days. The room goes quiet.

choices.text: Call them out: pistols at dawn
choices.result: At dawn the officer's shot goes wide. Yours takes the hat off their head. Honour satisfied, and a lesson learned.
choices.fail_result: You're hit, but you stood your ground. That counts for something here.

choices.result: Your answer has the whole room laughing at the officer instead.
choices.fail_result: Your answer falls flat. People will say you swallowed it.

life_hanging_speech.title: A last speech
life_hanging_speech.text: On the cart, one of the condemned looks out over the crowd, sees you, and shouts your name: an old shipmate, it seems, or someone who'd like the crowd to think so.

choices.result: The crowd turns to stare. A ballad about it will be sold by nightfall.
Behind you, the drop. Some of the crew saw you go.

life_fever_hospital.title: The fever hospital
life_fever_hospital.text: The friars' hospital is overflowing: fever patients on straw in the cloister, and not enough hands to carry water. The prior asks if your surgeon can help.

choices.text: Send your surgeon and a working party
choices.result: A week of hard work. The town won't forget the foreign ship that came to help.
choices.fail_result: The fever takes two of the working party. The town is grateful; your crew less so.

life_fever_crew.title: Fever ashore
life_fever_crew.text: The crew have seen the funerals. A deputation comes aft: they want to sail now, before the fever reaches the ship.

choices.text: Agree, and keep everyone aboard until you sail
choices.result: Nobody goes ashore. The relief is plain.

choices.text: Tell them the ship sails when you say so
choices.result: They go forward muttering, but they go.
choices.fail_result: One man jumps ship that night rather than wait.

life_captains_loan.title: A loan between captains
life_captains_loan.text: {cap} has had a bad cruise: a sprung mast, a crew owed wages, and creditors at the door. Over the second bottle comes the question: could you lend 200 gold, to be repaid from the next prize?

choices.result: {cap} grips your hand. You'll be repaid, they swear.
Half is better than nothing, and they know it.
{cap} shrugs. There are other captains.

life_loan_repaid.title: A debt repaid
life_loan_repaid.text: A letter finds you, with a heavy purse: {cap} has taken a fat prize, and pays back the loan with interest and thanks.

life_revolt_shore.title: On the beach
life_revolt_shore.text: Below the cliffs you find a group who have escaped the burning plantations: a dozen people with a dugout canoe that will never survive the open sea. Their leader speaks for them, steadily: they want passage off this island, and they will work for it.

choices.text: Offer them berths under the articles
choices.result: Most of them sign, for shares like anyone else; the rest ask to be put ashore down the coast, and you put them there. The planters will call you a thief; the crew call them shipmates.

choices.text: Give them provisions and a seaworthy boat
choices.result: Before they go, their leader tells you of a bay where the Maroons come down to trade with passing ships.

choices.text: Give them passage, wherever they ask
choices.result: They ask for the hills, where the Maroons live free, and their leader knows the bay where the Maroons come down to trade. Anchor there and they'll go up with the Maroons' guides.

life_revolt_harbour.title: An empty harbour
life_revolt_harbour.text: With the militia gone inland, the harbour of {port} is unguarded and in a panic. The governor's secretary is going from ship to ship asking captains to man the town's batteries.

choices.result: Your gunners stand watch on the walls for three nights. The town is grateful.

choices.text: Use the confusion: empty a planter's warehouse
choices.result: Nobody is watching the warehouses tonight. Somebody should have been.

life_procession.title: The procession
life_procession.text: The image of the saint sways past on the shoulders of the confraternity, gold leaf flashing in the candlelight. The whole street kneels. Some of your crew cross themselves.

choices.result: The town notices the foreign captain walking with the penitents.
Your name is read out at mass.

life_procession_thief.title: A light-fingered child
life_procession_thief.text: In the crush of the procession, a hand is in your pocket. Your quartermaster grabs the thief: {thief}, all elbows and bare feet, quick as an eel.

choices.text: Offer {thief} a place as ship's boy
choices.result: Quick hands are useful aboard. {thief} grins and comes along.
{thief} vanishes into the crowd before you've finished your lecture.

life_smugglers_buy.title: The night market
life_smugglers_buy.text: Lanterns on the sand, boats run up the beach, and bales of foreign cloth sold by torchlight at half what the shops ask. The customs house is dark.

choices.result: Cheap, if you can sell it where nobody asks where it came from.

choices.text: Tip off the customs (they pay informers)
choices.result: The soldiers come down the cliff path an hour later. The beach empties.

life_smugglers_sell.title: Buyers on the beach
life_smugglers_sell.text: The smugglers' buyers will take anything that can't be sold over a counter, and pay better than a fence. They've seen what's in your hold.

choices.result: Coin counted out by lantern light.

life_muster_commission.title: The governor's secretary
life_muster_commission.text: A harassed secretary behind a desk heaped with blank commissions. 'Captain. His Excellency needs every ship he can get against the enemy. Do you want a letter of marque, or have you come about something else?'

choices.text: Ask where the enemy's cruisers have been seen
choices.result: Reports from the coastguard and the fishing boats, a week old.

life_muster_veterans.title: Hands from the muster
life_muster_veterans.text: Privateers in port are poaching each other's crews. A gang of old hands, paid off from a ship that didn't sail, are looking for a captain with a reputation.

choices.result: Veterans of two wars, and they know it.

town_remembered.title: Welcome back to {port}
town_remembered.text: Your boat has barely touched the quay before someone calls your name. A fishwife presses a basket on the coxswain, a carter offers to haul your water for nothing, and three young men off the waterfront ask if the {ship} needs hands.

choices.result: The crew eat well tonight, and walk a little taller.
They're aboard before you've finished speaking.

town_grudge.title: {port} has not forgotten
town_grudge.text: The chandler shuts up shop as you come up the quay. Children throw stones at your boat, a woman spits, and in the church the priest is saying a mass for those who died by your hand.

choices.text: Pay for masses for the dead
choices.result: The priest takes your money without looking at you. But the stones stop.

choices.text: Pay what the chandler asks, and more
choices.result: The chandler serves you at twice the price, eyes on the floor.
They scatter. Your crew don't enjoy being hated.

choices.text: Kneel at the back of the church and hear the mass for the dead
choices.result: Heads turn. Nobody speaks to you. But the next morning the chandler opens his shop.
